topic.title: Destination wedding filter
topic.claim: A destination wedding isn't about the view; it's a polite way to shrink the guest list without uninviting anyone.
topic.moment: The Udaipur wedding where half the relatives 'just couldn't make it.'

turn.believed: The couple wanted a scenic, special celebration.
turn.actually: Distance and cost quietly remove the guests you didn't want, and nobody has to be cut.

topic.because: guests at a destination wedding usually pay for flights, leave and outfits while the hosts cover the hotel, so distance quietly filters out the relatives who aren't close
topic.payoff: A destination wedding is the softest 'you're not invited' ever invented.
topic.behaviour: Families pick far-off venues partly to keep numbers and obligations down.
topic.mechanism: The airfare cuts the guest list so the host doesn't have to.
topic.group: Couples and families planning weddings, and the relatives who feel the distance
topic.send_to: A cousin planning a 'small intimate' wedding somewhere expensive.
topic.why_now: Destination weddings keep rising and the guest lists keep shrinking.

cover.headline: A destination wedding [uninvites] the relatives you didn't want
cover.sub: Half of them 'just couldn't make it.' Funny, which half.

paragraphs: A destination wedding isn't really about the view. It removes the guests you didn't want, and nobody ever has to say so.
slides.why_swipe: How does a venue remove guests? The reader wants the trick.

paragraphs: The wedding is in Udaipur. The hosts cover the hotel by the lake. You just need flights for two, three days of leave and outfits for four functions.
And suddenly half the relatives 'just couldn't make it.' Work came up. Kids' exams. Something always comes up.
slides.why_swipe: Why did exactly those people drop out, and not the others?

paragraphs: Everyone says the couple wanted something scenic. But look at who vanished: never the inner circle, always the far edge of the family.
**Flights, leave and four outfits did the cutting.** Not a single name had to be struck off.
slides.why_swipe: so how does the far edge leave without anyone saying a word?

paragraphs: No aunty is told she wasn't wanted. She removes herself, politely, on WhatsApp: "beta, itni door yaar."
The couple gets the smaller crowd without one awkward phone call.

end.save: Open this again the next time a 'small, intimate' wedding somewhere expensive lands in your chats.
end.send: Send to a cousin planning a 'small intimate' wedding in a hill fort.

draft.caption: Think about the last destination wedding you skipped. Was it the flight, or did you both already know you weren't that close?
draft.alt_text: A six-slide text post arguing that a destination wedding is a polite way to shrink the guest list. Because flights and a three-night stay cost money, the relatives the couple was never close to quietly stay home, so the host controls the numbers and the budget without ever uninviting anyone.

ledger.text: Because destination weddings require guests to pay for flights, take leave, and buy multiple outfits, and these costs fall hardest on distant relatives rather than close family, destination weddings function as a socially acceptable way to shrink the guest list without ever explicitly uninviting anyone
ledger.sentence: A destination wedding isn't really about the view. It removes the guests you didn't want, and nobody ever has to say so.

mechanism.broken_premise: None fully breaks. The weakest link is 'these costs fall hardest on distant relatives' — flights/leave/outfits cost close and distant guests roughly the same in absolute terms; what differs is each guest's willingness to bear that cost relative to how close they feel. So the filter runs on the guest's own cost-benefit threshold, not on costs being heavier for distant relatives.
mechanism.actual_mechanism: In Indian destination weddings the host typically covers the hotel, meals and local transfers but guests pay their own flights, leave and outfits, so attending carries a real per-guest price that is independent of closeness. Distant relatives, for whom the trip isn't 'worth it,' decline on their own citing distance or work, which lets the host end up with a smaller, closer crowd without striking a single name — though the host also caps numbers directly through venue capacity and which guests get paid rooms, so self-selection is one layer on top of that, not the whole story.

sources.quote: Guests book their own flights, while the couple handles accommodation, food, and local transport.
For 100 guests, the per-head cost ranges from ₹18,000 to ₹40,000; the per-head figure drops as guest lists grow because fixed spending is shared by more people.
Ideal guest counts for destination weddings range from 80 to 150 guests, though destination weddings typically have 100–300 guests.
